components.note: 亻 (person) — a person
犬 (dog) — a dog lying low, the image of crouching or hiding

example.pinyin: Tā fú zài zhuōzi shang shuìzháo le.
example.english: He fell asleep slumped over the desk.
example.fact: 伏 appears in 起伏 (ups and downs), 伏击 (ambush) and 伏特 (volt). 三伏天, the hottest stretch of summer, is the 'dog days' of the Chinese calendar.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — baskets were woven from bamboo
监 (jiān) offers a loose sound hint for lán

example.hanzi: 她提着一个篮子去买菜。
example.pinyin: Tā tí zhe yí gè lánzi qù mǎicài.
example.english: She carries a basket to buy groceries.
example.fact: 篮 gives 篮子 (basket) and 篮球 (basketball, literally 'basket ball'). 菜篮子 is also a common way to refer to a city's food supply.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — striking or attacking
工 (gōng) gives the sound — an exact match

example.english: Our team is attacking.
example.fact: 攻 has two common uses: attack (进攻, 攻击) and intensive study (攻读 a degree). In modern slang, 攻略 means a walkthrough or travel guide, as in 旅游攻略.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — body part; the upper 户 is only loosely related

example.english: His shoulders are broad.
example.fact: 肩 often takes 膀 in speech (肩膀). It also means 'to bear', as in 肩负 (shoulder a responsibility), and gives 双肩包 (backpack).

components.note: 口 (mouth) — biting or speaking
丁 (dīng) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Wǒ bèi wénzi dīng le yíxià.
example.english: I was bitten by a mosquito.
example.fact: 叮 covers insect bites (被蚊子叮) and pressing someone (叮嘱, 'to instruct repeatedly'). 叮咚 is the sound of a bell or drops of water.

components.note: The origin is debated, often read as a knotted cord; the shape was borrowed to write 'self' and the sixth Heavenly Stem.

example.english: You should believe in yourself.
example.fact: 己 almost always appears in 自己 (oneself), 知己 (a soulmate) and the Confucian line 己所不欲，勿施于人. Don't confuse it with 已 (yǐ) and 巳 (sì): 己 is open at the top, 已 half closed, 巳 fully closed.

components.note: A vine curling around a melon hanging at its base.

example.english: In summer I like to eat watermelon.
example.fact: 瓜 covers the melon and gourd family: 西瓜 (watermelon), 黄瓜 (cucumber), 南瓜 (pumpkin). 吃瓜群众 ('melon-eating crowd') is slang for bystanders watching gossip.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — reaching in with the hand
匋 (táo) gives the sound — a near match

example.pinyin: Tā cóng kǒudài lǐ tāochū shǒujī.
example.english: He pulled his phone out of his pocket.
example.fact: 掏 is colloquial. 掏钱 means 'to pay up', also 掏腰包; 掏耳朵 is to clean your ears; 掏心窝 means to speak from the heart.

components.note: 人 (person) — a person with strokes at each side, standing between two points

example.hanzi: 请允许我介绍一下自己。
example.pinyin: Qǐng yǔnxǔ wǒ jièshào yíxià zìjǐ.
example.english: Please allow me to introduce myself.
example.fact: 介 appears in 介绍 (introduce), 介意 (to mind, as in 别介意), 中介 (agent) and 媒介 (medium). It is also a measure word in the literary 一介书生 ('a mere scholar').

components.note: 鬼 (ghost) — spirits
云 (yún) gives the sound — a near match

example.pinyin: Tā xià de hún dōu fēi le.
example.english: He was so scared his soul flew out of him.
example.fact: 魂 is the ethereal soul. Traditional thought pairs it with 魄 (the bodily soul). 灵魂 is 'soul', 丢魂 'lose one's wits', and 魂 also appears in 民族魂 ('soul of a nation').

components.note: 钅 (metal) — keys and bolts are metal
建 (jiàn) gives the sound — an exact match

example.english: Please press this key.
example.fact: 键 is the key of a keyboard or piano, and gives 键盘 (keyboard), 按键 (button) and 化学键 (chemical bond). 关键 (the crucial point) uses it in a different sense.

components.note: 心 (heart) — loyalty comes from the heart
中 (zhōng) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Zhè zhī gǒu duì zhǔrén hěn zhōngxīn.
example.english: This dog is very loyal to its master.
example.fact: 忠 is the Confucian virtue of loyalty, often paired with 孝 (filial piety). 忠诚 is 'loyal', 忠告 is 'advice', and 忠言逆耳 ('honest words grate on the ear') is a saying.

components.note: ⺼ (meat) — the offering
寸 (hand) — holding it up
示 (altar) — the place of sacrifice

example.hanzi: 清明节我们去祭拜祖先。
example.pinyin: Qīngmíng jié wǒmen qù jìbài zǔxiān.
example.english: On Qingming we go to pay respects to our ancestors.
example.fact: 祭 shows up in 祭祖 (ancestor worship), 祭品 (offerings), 祭坛 (altar). As a surname it is read Zhài.

components.note: 氵 (water) — depth of water
戋 (jiān) gives a sound hint shared with 钱, 线 and 战

example.hanzi: 这条河很浅，孩子也能走过去。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo hé hěn qiǎn, háizi yě néng zǒu guòqù.
example.english: This river is shallow; even a child could wade across.
example.fact: 浅 is the opposite of 深. It describes colours (浅蓝 light blue), and ideas (肤浅 superficial, 浅显 easy to grasp).

components.note: 页 (head) — turning the head to look
厄 (è) is a simplified stand-in giving only a rough sound hint

example.hanzi: 她一个人照顾三个孩子。
example.pinyin: Tā yí gè rén zhàogù sān gè háizi.
example.english: She looks after three children on her own.
example.fact: 顾 appears in 照顾 (take care of), 顾客 (customer), 回顾 (look back) and 顾虑 (misgiving).

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — an organ
旦 (dàn) gives the sound — differs only in tone

example.english: This child is very bold.
example.fact: In Chinese, courage is 'a big gall bladder': 大胆 (bold), 胆小 (timid) and 胆子 (nerve). 卧薪尝胆 comes from the story of a king who tasted gall to remember his humiliation.

components.note: 歹 (bad, death) — damage and death
戋 (jiān) gives a loose sound hint

example.english: He has a leg disability.
example.fact: 残 means damaged or remaining: 残疾 (disability), 残留 (residue), 残忍 (cruel), 残酷 (brutal). 残废 is now often considered impolite.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hands thrown forward
卜 (bǔ) gives the sound — a near match

example.pinyin: Xiǎo gǒu xiàng wǒ pū guòlái.
example.english: The puppy pounced at me.
example.fact: 扑 includes 扑克 (poker), 扑灭 (to put out) and 扑面而来 ('to rush at your face'). 扑通 is the sound of a splash.

components.note: 风 (wind) — floating on the wind
票 (piào) gives the sound — a near match

example.english: White clouds drift across the sky.
example.fact: 飘 is used for things carried by wind: 飘雪 (drifting snow), 飘香 (fragrance wafting). In slang, 飘了 means to get too cocky, 'to get carried away'.

components.note: 王 (jade) — jewels and treasure; the right-hand part is a reduced 㐱 offering only a rough sound hint

example.english: We should cherish our time.
example.fact: 珍 is a bound form: 珍惜 (cherish), 珍贵 (precious), 珍珠 (pearl), 山珍海味 (delicacies from the mountains and the sea). 珍重 is also a parting word, 'take care'.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — visiting involves talking
方 (fāng) gives the sound — differs in the tone

example.english: The reporter interviewed him today.
example.fact: 访 is bound: 访问 (visit), 采访 (interview), 拜访 (call on), 访客 (visitor). 拜访 is respectful, used when visiting someone of higher status.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — calling out
刀 (dāo) gives a loose sound hint

example.english: The teacher called everyone together for a meeting.
example.fact: 召 is formal and appears in 召开 (to convene), 召唤 (summon), 号召 (call upon) and 召回 (recall a product).

components.note: 氵 (water) — thirst is for water
曷 (hé) offers a loose sound hint

example.english: I'm both thirsty and hungry.
example.fact: 渴 also means longing, in 渴望 (to long for) and 渴求. 口渴 is 'thirsty', and the idiom 临渴掘井 means 'dig a well only when thirsty'.

meanings: to be born in the year of

components.note: 尸 (body, corpse) — an old person-like shape
禹 (yǔ) gives a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Wǒ shǔ lóng, nǐ shǔ shénme?
example.english: I'm a dragon; what are you?
example.fact: 你属什么? is how Chinese people ask someone's zodiac sign. 属于 means 'to belong to', 金属 is 'metal'. It can also be read zhǔ, in literary words.

components.note: 木 (wood) — a branch or handle
可 (kě) gives the sound — an exact match

example.english: Mr. Ke is not here today.
example.fact: 柯 is mostly a surname and a transliteration character: 柯南 (Conan), 柯达 (Kodak). In classical texts it means an axe handle, and 伐柯 stands for matchmaking.

excludeSuggestion: mostly appears as a surname or in transliterated names

components.note: A person bowing, as the old graph is traditionally read; its early meaning was 'clan'.

example.english: This surname is quite rare.
example.fact: 氏 is a bound form. 姓氏 is 'surname', and 摄氏度 (Celsius) and 华氏度 (Fahrenheit) use 氏 after the scientist's surname. Anciently 氏 marked a clan branch while 姓 marked the lineage.

components.note: 力 (strength) — effort
堇 (jǐn) offers a loose sound hint

example.english: He studies very diligently.
example.fact: 勤 is seen in 勤奋 (diligent), 勤快 (hardworking, colloquial), 出勤 (attendance), 后勤 (logistics). 勤能补拙 means 'diligence can make up for lack of talent'.

components.note: 女 (woman) — a female relative
且 (qiě) offers a loose sound hint

example.english: My older sister works in Beijing.
example.fact: 姐 is used for older sisters, and also affectionately for an older female friend or colleague. 小姐 is 'Miss', but in mainland usage it can carry unfortunate overtones, so 女士 is safer.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — restraints are metal
考 (kǎo) gives the sound — an exact match

example.hanzi: 警察给小偷戴上了手铐。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá gěi xiǎotōu dài shàng le shǒukào.
example.english: The police put handcuffs on the thief.
example.fact: 铐 mostly occurs in 手铐 (handcuffs), and as a verb meaning to handcuff, as in 铐住. 脚镣 is the word for leg shackles.

components.note: 车 (cart) — the older form 轟 had three carts, the sound of rumbling wheels

example.pinyin: Yuǎnchù chuánlái hōng de yì shēng.
example.english: A boom came from the distance.
example.fact: 轰 imitates an explosion: 轰炸 (bombing), 轰动 (to cause a sensation), 轰隆 (rumble). Colloquially, 轰走 means to chase someone away.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a hall or building
申 (shēn) gives the sound — differs in the final

example.english: The judge is hearing the case.
example.fact: 审 appears in 审判 (trial), 审查 (review), 审核 (audit), 审美 (aesthetics). 审美疲劳 means 'aesthetic fatigue'.

components.note: 氵 (water) — crossing water
度 (dù) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Wǒmen zuò chuán dùguò le hé.
example.english: We crossed the river by boat.
example.fact: 渡 means crossing water, as in 渡口 (ferry crossing), 摆渡 (ferry), and figuratively 渡过难关 (get through a hard time).

components.note: 阝 (city) — a place or station
由 (yóu) gives the sound — an exact match

example.english: I'm going to the post office to send a letter.
example.fact: 邮 gives 邮局 (post office), 邮票 (stamp), 邮件 (mail, email) and 邮寄 (to post). It originally meant a relay station.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — the older sense was a bow drawn fully
尔 (ěr) gives a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Tā xiǎng míbǔ zìjǐ de cuòwù.
example.english: He wants to make up for his mistake.
example.fact: 弥 appears in 弥补 (make up for), 弥漫 (to spread), 弥天大谎 (a whopping lie). 阿弥陀佛 is the Buddhist invocation.

components.note: 见 (see) — pleasing to see
青 (qīng) offers a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Tā jīntiān chuān de hěn liàng.
example.english: She's dressed beautifully today.
example.fact: 靓 comes from Cantonese 靚. 靓仔 is 'handsome guy' and 靓女 'pretty girl', 靓丽 means beautiful. The old dictionary reading jìng is now rare.

components.note: 木 (wood) — a tree or stick
口 (ring) — the ring tied around it as a bundle

example.pinyin: Tā sòng le wǒ yí shù huā.
example.english: He gave me a bunch of flowers.
example.fact: 束 is a measure word for flowers, beams of light and bundles: 一束花, 一束光. It is also in 结束 (finish), 约束 (restrain) and 束缚 (to bind).

components.note: 讠 (speech) — a spoken exclamation
矣 (yǐ) offers a loose sound hint

example.english: Hey, look over there!
example.fact: 诶 is a written form of 欸, an interjection that changes meaning with tone: ēi (hey), éi (huh?), ěi (what?) and èi (yes). It's most common in chat and informal writing.

components.note: 彳 (step) — walking, conduct
聿 (yù, a brush) — the writing of rules

example.english: You should obey the law.
example.fact: 律 gives 法律 (law), 律师 (lawyer), 纪律 (discipline), 规律 (pattern), 一律 (all alike) and 旋律 (melody).

components.note: Traditionally explained as an inverted 予 ('to give'), used for something unreal that is given and taken away.

example.english: He likes watching sci-fi movies.
example.fact: 幻 appears in 科幻 (sci-fi), 幻想 (fantasy), 幻觉 (hallucination), 梦幻 (dreamy). 幻灯片 is a slide, e.g. in a presentation.

components.note: Three flowing lines picturing a stream running between its banks.

example.english: Sichuan food is very spicy.
example.fact: 川 is also the short name for Sichuan, 'the four rivers'. 川菜 is Sichuan cuisine, and 川 appears in 山川 (mountains and rivers).

components.note: 扌 (hand) — reaching into water
劳 (láo) gives the sound — an exact match

example.hanzi: 他把掉进水里的手机捞了出来。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ diào jìn shuǐ lǐ de shǒujī lāo le chūlái.
example.english: He fished the phone out of the water.
example.fact: 捞 is colloquial: 打捞 (salvage), 捞一把 (to grab a profit), 捞钱 (to make money, often dishonestly).

components.note: 足 (foot) — striding
夸 (kuā) gives the sound — differs in the tone

example.pinyin: Tā kuàguò le nà tiáo xiǎo hé.
example.english: He stepped over the little stream.
example.fact: 跨 now spans 'across' in many modern words: 跨国 (multinational), 跨境 (cross-border), 跨年 (to ring in the New Year) and 跨界 (crossover).

components.note: 衤 (clothing) — a garment
君 (jūn) gives the sound — a near match

example.pinyin: Tā chuānzhe yì tiáo hóng qúnzi.
example.english: She is wearing a red skirt.
example.fact: The measure word is 条: 一条裙子. 连衣裙 is a dress. 裙带关系 ('skirt-belt relationship') means nepotism.

components.note: 饣 (food) — a place serving meals
官 (guān) gives the sound — a near match

example.english: We're going to the library at the weekend.
example.fact: 馆 is used as a suffix for public places: 图书馆 (library), 博物馆 (museum), 饭馆 (restaurant), 宾馆 (hotel). 下馆子 means 'to eat out'.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a cry
敖 (áo) gives the sound — an exact match

example.english: The puppy is whimpering with hunger.
example.fact: 嗷 imitates crying. 嗷嗷待哺 (like hungry nestlings waiting to be fed) is an idiom for people in desperate need.

components.note: 衣 (clothing) — the old sense was the hem of a robe, the far edge, extended to distant descendants

example.english: He is an American of Chinese descent.
example.fact: 裔 appears in 华裔 (a foreign national of Chinese descent), 后裔 (descendants), 亚裔 (Asian-descent) and 非裔 (African-descent). 华侨 refers to Chinese citizens living abroad.

components.note: Simplified from 縣, which is the old source of 悬 'to hang'.

example.pinyin: Wǒ jiā zài yí gè xiǎo xiànchéng lǐ.
example.english: My home is in a small county town.
example.fact: 县 is the administrative unit below prefecture, and 县城 is a county seat. Counties date back over two thousand years.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — a sudden storm
隹 (short-tailed bird) — birds startled into flight

example.pinyin: Huò xiānsheng shì wǒ de lǎoshī.
example.english: Mr. Huo is my teacher.
example.fact: 霍 is mostly a surname: 霍去病 (Han general), and in transliteration 霍金 (Hawking). In 霍乱 it means cholera and 霍然 is 'suddenly'.

excludeSuggestion: mostly a surname or used in transliterations

components.note: 黑 (black) — the colour of the pigment
代 (dài) gives the sound — an exact match

example.hanzi: 林黛玉是《红楼梦》里的人物。
example.pinyin: Lín Dàiyù shì Hónglóumèng lǐ de rénwù.
example.english: Lin Daiyu is a character in Dream of the Red Chamber.
example.fact: 黛 was a pigment for painting eyebrows, so 粉黛 ('powder and brow-pigment') stands for women. It is best known in the name of Lin Daiyu.

excludeSuggestion: literary; mostly seen in names such as 黛玉

components.note: 舟 (boat) — ships
亢 (kàng) offers a loose sound hint

example.english: This flight is delayed.
example.fact: 航 originally meant a boat; now it covers flights and ships: 航班 (flight), 航空 (aviation), 航海 (sailing), 导航 (navigation) and 航天 (spaceflight).
